comment: Third-party sources the Windows (Kainote.sln) build fetches as archives.
Most third-party code is a git submodule instead -- see Thirdparty/README.md.
These five stay archives because a submodule would not work or would not pay:
fribidi  its git tag ships none of the generated lib/*.tab.i tables or
fribidi-unicode-version.h that the build's sources #include; only
the release tarball has them pre-generated.
boost    the git repository is a ~500 MB tree of nested submodules.
icu      likewise very large, and only source/common + source/i18n are used.
zlib     small enough that an archive is simpler.
Run Thirdparty/hydrate.ps1 to fetch these. It verifies each archive's SHA-256
before extracting and refuses to continue on a mismatch.
To bump one: change version+url, then put the new archive's SHA-256 in sha256
The Linux build (CMakeLists.txt) ignores this file entirely; it resolves every
one of these through pkg-config against the distribution's packages.

dependencies.name: fribidi
dependencies.note: Must be the release tarball, not a git archive: it ships the pre-generated lib/*.tab.i tables.
